clue.text: Opposed to colleague being on call endlessly, in responsive manner

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece being on another follows it, so the colleague comes after the call

parts.note: anti means against, opposed to

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for call loses its final letter

parts.note: to call someone is to phone them
an ally is a colleague or partner

explanation.surface: Someone who dislikes having a colleague forever on the phone answers in kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposed to' reads like part of the definition but supplies the first piece; 'endlessly' drops the final letter of the telephone word, and 'being on' places the colleague after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphonal singing alternates between two groups, each answering the other, so it is a responsive style.

clue.text: Go and bat — no opener to lead on

indicators.note: no opener says the word bat loses its first letter

parts.note: to tempt someone is to lead them on

explanation.surface: A cricketer is told to go in and bat, though the first batsman is not to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no opener' trims BAT to AT. 'Opener' also suggests a cricket opening batsman, a false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A go is an attempt, as in 'have a go' meaning try.

clue.text: Proud King Rat elevated one in five

indicators.note: elevated in a down clue means lifted upward, so the word rat reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a quin is one of quintuplets, five babies born together

explanation.surface: An arrogant monarch promotes a rodent to be one of a set of five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns RAT into TAR in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarquinius Superbus, 'the Proud', was the last king of Rome.

clue.text: Tree breaks as I chop it

indicators.note: breaks signals the following words are smashed up and reformed

explanation.surface: A tree splits apart as a woodcutter swings the axe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges AS I CHOP IT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pistachio is a small tree of the cashew family whose green nuts are eaten.

clue.text: Excel in society, just as before

parts.note: a debutante who has come out has entered society
do is short for ditto, meaning the same as before

explanation.surface: To shine socially, just as one did previously.
explanation.walkthrough: DO, as in 'ditto', marks a repeat of what was written above.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo rivals is to surpass them, which is to excel over them.

clue.text: Charms a stubborn person with extremes of tenderness

parts.note: a mule is a stubborn person, after the obstinate animal

indicators.note: extremes of means the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone wins over an obstinate person by being very tender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremes of' takes T and S, the first and last letters of tenderness.
explanation.definitionFit: Amulets are lucky charms worn to ward off harm.

clue.text: The French show fight against the Turks

parts.note: le is French for the
a panto, short for pantomime, is a Christmas stage show in Britain

explanation.surface: French forces demonstrate they will battle the Ottoman Turks.
explanation.walkthrough: A PANTO is a British family stage comedy staged around Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1571 naval battle there saw the Holy League defeat the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: Excellent position close to game

explanation.surface: A strong place to be when the match is nearly won.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis the score after deuce is 'advantage', also called vantage, one point from winning the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A good spot for viewing is a commanding viewpoint; in tennis, advantage is the score just short of winning the game.

clue.text: Insects are found inside one of the Scorpion group

indicators.note: found inside tells us the word are sits within the insects

parts.note: ants are insects

explanation.surface: Bugs turn up within a constellation shaped like a scorpion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found inside' is the container signal. The Scorpion group is the constellation Scorpius, whose brightest star is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the brightest star in the constellation Scorpius, the Scorpion.

clue.text: Loudly proclaim harlot's execution

indicators.note: execution here means beheading, so the word for harlot loses its head letter

parts.note: a strumpet is an old word for a harlot

explanation.surface: A town crier announces that a prostitute is to be hanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'execution' is a beheading: STRUMPET loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet something is to announce it noisily, as a herald with a horn would.

clue.text: Habitue of platform involved in apt retorts

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A regular on a stage gets mixed up in sharp exchanges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges IN APT RETORTS. A trainspotter is a British hobbyist who notes down the numbers of passing locomotives.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway enthusiasts who log engine numbers spend hours standing on station platforms.

clue.text: For Tokyo course, need re-drawn map? True

indicators.note: a map that is re-drawn has its letters set out anew, here along with true

explanation.surface: A diner in Japan is told the map must be redrawn, and agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-drawn' rearranges MAP and TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempura, battered fried fish or vegetables, is a classic dish served as a course in Japan.

clue.text: Pacific group, but at war in, say'. 1984

explanation.surface: A peaceful island group finds itself fighting in a particular year.
explanation.walkthrough: 1984 is Orwell's novel, in which the superstate of that name is permanently at war; 'Pacific' looks like 'peaceful', clashing with 'at war'.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers the islands of the Pacific region, and is also the superstate in Orwell's novel that is always fighting Eurasia or Eastasia.

clue.text: Board make progress

explanation.surface: Climb aboard and get moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To board a bus is to climb onto it; to advance or prosper is also to do well in this phrasal sense.

clue.text: Easily passes on

explanation.surface: Someone wins comfortably and gives things to the next generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning without effort is winning in a walk; bequeathing heirlooms to descendants is giving them along a family line.

clue.text: Stark attitude of keen and reformed Nazis

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of keen and are rearranged

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A severe outlook among keen former Nazis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' rearranges KEEN AND into NAKEDNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stark naked describes being completely bare, so the state of having no clothes on is this.

clue.text: Thrust forward, but fall before double attack

indicators.note: before puts the word for fall ahead of the word for double attack

parts.note: to pitch is to fall headlong
in chess a fork is one piece attacking two at once

explanation.surface: A soldier lunges ahead but stumbles before attacking twice.
explanation.walkthrough: A fork is a chess term: a single piece threatening two enemy pieces at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitchfork someone is to push them abruptly into a position, as hay is tossed with a farm tool.

clue.text: Elizabethan computer's prayer-scarf?

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Elizabethan computer's prayer-scarf?'; the scan prints 'Elizabethan compotner'th prayer-scarf?', garbled in the key word, so the wordplay cannot be recovered.

clue.text: Florence Nightingale, say, had drug to hand

indicators.note: to means added to, putting the drug before the hand

parts.note: heroin is a drug
in bridge the four hands are North, East, South and West, so E is a hand

explanation.surface: A celebrated nurse kept medication ready at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points, so 'hand' gives E for East. 'had' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence Nightingale is a celebrated example of a brave woman admired for her deeds.

clue.text: Classify as mature, but lacking wife

indicators.note: lacking tells us the abbreviation for wife is taken away

parts.note: to grow up is to mature

explanation.surface: Someone sorted as an adult, though still single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes W out of GROW UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To group things is to sort them into categories, which is classifying them.

clue.text: How gamekeeper begins to discover grouse

indicators.note: how a word begins is its first letter, so we take the opening letter of gamekeeper

parts.note: to rumble someone is to discover or see through them

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper sets out to find game birds on the moor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'begins' takes G from gamekeeper. 'grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb 'complain'.
explanation.definitionFit: To grouse is to complain, which is to grumble.

clue.text: French city where one may find gold? Depends

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
to lean on is to depend, so leans means depends

explanation.surface: A French town where treasure might be found depends on luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Orleans is a city on the Loire, famous for Joan of Arc.

clue.text: Wrongly flippant about where Viola was wrecked

parts.note: ill can mean badly or wrongly, as in ill-advised

indicators.note: about signals the word for flippant is turned round

parts.note: airy means light and flippant

explanation.surface: A careless remark about a shipwreck in Shakespeare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AIRY into YRIA. Viola is the heroine of Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, shipwrecked at its opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelfth Night opens with Viola washed ashore on the coast of this ancient Adriatic region.

clue.text: Coins belonging to the girl from the Five Towns

definitions.text: belonging to the girl from the Five Towns

explanation.surface: Money owned by a young woman from the Potteries.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold Bennett's novel 'Anna of the Five Towns' is set in the Staffordshire Potteries; the possessive of her name means belonging to her.
explanation.definitionFit: Annas were former Indian coins, sixteen to the rupee; Bennett's Anna is the girl of the Five Towns, so something of hers is hers.

clue.text: Old garment, seen in cotton

parts.note: an Elizabethan jacket is the plain sense; the second reading is what the letters of cotton show in their middle, a pair of Ts described as a phrase

explanation.surface: An antique piece of clothing turns up made of cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of cotton contain TT in the middle, which said as words gives the answer; the garment is the straight reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men in Tudor and Elizabethan times.

clue.text: Guesswork — but not in teaching

indicators.note: not says the word in is dropped from the word for guesswork

parts.note: intuition is knowing by instinct, a kind of guesswork

explanation.surface: Learning is about more than inspired guessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes IN from the front of INTUITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is instruction given by a tutor, which is teaching.

clue.text: Pair reject me at first, then are welcoming

indicators.note: at first puts the turned-round word at the front, ahead of the pair
to reject is to throw back, so the word me is turned round

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of pheasants

explanation.surface: A couple turn someone down at first and then warm to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reject' turns the word me round and 'at first' puts it ahead of the pair. The definition is plural, matching a subject such as 'they'.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace people or ideas is to welcome them warmly, so those who do so are greeting them.

clue.text: The stage version of The Brontes?

definitions.text: The stage version of The Brontes?

parts.words: The stage version of The Brontes?
parts.note: Charlotte, Emily and Anne were a trio of siblings, and a Chekhov play has that very description as its title

explanation.surface: A theatre adaptation of the famous literary family from Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontes were Charlotte, Emily and Anne; Chekhov's play about the Prozorov siblings has the matching title.
explanation.definitionFit: Chekhov's drama about the Prozorov siblings bears this title, which also describes the trio of Bronte novelists.
